title: Greenville Commerce Journal: CEO Video, Layoffs, "$2.6M Loss"

fields.subject: Comment by 17:00 ET – CEO video, Spartanburg layoffs, $2.6M loss?
fields.body:
Hello,

I'm writing about a video circulating on Clipwave in which your CEO appears to announce a Querétaro acquisition and layoffs in Spartanburg. The post I'm looking at had close to 10,000 views a few minutes ago, and Spartanburg employees are already sharing it with us.

Separately, a source tells me Tamarack "lost $2.6 million to a deepfake wire scam today" and that the FBI is "taking over."

On the record, please:

1) Is the video authentic?
2) Are Spartanburg jobs being cut?
3) Did Tamarack lose $2.6 million, and is the FBI involved?

I file at 17:00 ET for our evening business update. If I don't hear back, the story will say Tamarack did not respond by deadline. A call is fine if that's quicker.

Thanks,

instructorNote: This is a pressure inject. When you hand it over, read aloud that the Spartanburg switchboard has logged 14 employee calls in 10 minutes. Also read the second-shift lead's text to Comms: "The video is on everyone's phone. People are walking off the line to watch it. What do I tell them?" Watch for these steps: Comms starts the 60-minute TEIVES 4 holding-statement clock from 16:20 and uses "looking into a video brought to our attention" until the CEO confirms. The statement does not repeat the layoff claim or confirm acquisition talks. It uses no loss figure except the Controller's signed numbers ($2.64M was requested, not lost), with the CFO approving any figure. Legal limits the law-enforcement line to "we have reported the matter to the FBI." Spartanburg staff get their message no later than the public statement.
